messages:
anya: Heads up from GTM: Prospect RFP calls out CompetitorY 'Embeddings Mini' - 40% lower cost, claims 2x index throughput. They're asking for a concrete response by EOW.

mike: Can someone capture the exact spec? dims, batch, quant, index tricks? We need to call out where their offering deviates.

jo: Link from AE: https://example.com/competitory-mini. Key notes: 512-d only, uses aggressive PQ + a managed ANN index. No support for streaming or per-request tool calls.

cory: So their price looks attractive, but they constrain dims + index type. That will hurt some of our customers who need 2048 or fine-grained vectors.

evan: Ops note: they avoid high-memory models by precomputing compressed vectors server-side. That explains throughput claims.

anya: Sales asks two things: 1) a short rebuttal/comparison doc for bids, 2) a product decision: pursue a parity SKU or highlight our superior guarantees (quality, latency predictability, console features).

mike: Proposal from eng: build a "Mini" SKU that exposes a 512-d quantized model + lower SLAs to hit price parity. Rough estimate: 1 sprint spike, 3 sprints for hardened rollout. Maintenance cost unknown.

jo: Counter-proposal: Assemble a customer-facing kit that emphasizes 'Production-grade embeddings' - include benchmarks (embed quality metrics), observability screenshots, and migration notes. Low lift; immediate.

cory: Business asks: if we don't match price, will customers churn? Sales says up to 2 pilots could walk unless we offer short-term discounts.

evan: Risk assessment: launching a cheaper SKU increases surface area (billing, console UI, routing, monitoring). Also fragmentation of eval metrics.

anya: Thinking hybrid approach: immediate tactical GTM (discounts + compare sheet) + short spike to validate the 512-quant variant. If spike passes quality gates we can decide to expose it.

mike: Quality gates for spike (technical): 1) embedding cosine correlation >= 0.98 on our internal retrieval set 2) P95 latency delta <= 8ms for <=64 token queries 3) memory down >= 35% on inference nodes.

jo: Product/Business gates: 1) AE sign-off that price delta likely closes renewal 2) SRE acceptance on isolation/ops cost 3) Console UX for tier visibility and migration docs ready.

cory: If spike fails, fallback: formal discount program + tailored migration assistance. If spike succeeds, pilot with 1 customer for 14 days with enhanced monitoring.

evan: Monitoring hooks we need: per-tenant embedding quality sampling, drift alarms (cosine drop), and auto-fallback to full model when thresholds hit. I'll draft the monitoring checklist.

deploy-bot: repo: embeddings-mini-spike branch created by mike at 1762610022.

anya: Owners: mike (eng spike + rollout path), jo (product docs + GTM kit), cory (commercial terms + pilot coordination), evan (evals + monitoring). I'll write a one-pager PRD-lite and share for review.

mike: Eng notes: prefer to run the spike on a canary pool to isolate resource profile. Need infra sign-off for dedicated autoscale knobs if we ship this SKU.

jo: For GTM one-pager: I'll include a competitor FAQ, recommended talking points, a decision tree for customers (when to choose Redwood full vs Mini), and suggested discount language for renewals.

cory: Legal: any special terms? I'll loop in legal for a short-term discount contract addendum.

evan: I'll assemble eval datasets today: retrieval-bench, semantic-ops, and at least one customer dataset (with consent). Need access: jo can coordinate.

anya: Timeline: Day 0: publish compare sheet + temporary discount playbook. Day 2: spike kickoff. Day 8: spike results + decision. Day 20: if green, pilot with 1-2 customers for 14 days.

jo: Sales wants the compare sheet by EOD tomorrow. cory, can you give them a template discount (duration, % range, commitment)?

cory: I'll propose an initial range: 20-30% for 3 month commitment or a usage-based rebate, pending legal.

mike: Small engineering caveat: if we expose a lower-tier SKU we must label it clearly in Console ("cost-optimized - lower dim/quality") and provide migration notes for retraining indexes. Don't want silent regressions.

evan: Agreed. Also include per-tenant quality telemetry visible to customers so they can see degradation risk.

anya: Decision for this thread: proceed with hybrid plan (GTM rebuttal + spike). Owners assigned above. If anyone objects, flag now.

jo: no objections. I'll start the one-pager.

cory: no objections. looping legal now.

mike: starting crate for spike tests; will post runbook link.

evan: prepping eval harness.

anya: thanks team. I'll post PRD-lite and deck link when ready. :rocket:
